description.narrative:
Implementing strategy YRDP (co-applicant) focuses on promoting and engaging young people in utilising mobile and online platforms for civic engagement, and on building their capacity to engage at the sub-national level. YRDP will support partners in effectively mobilising and engaging youth in local civic engagement, drawing on its experience and expertise. YRDP is unique in enabling youth and communities to act democratically. YRDP has expertise in youth empowerment, mobilisation and participation in promoting civic education and civic actions. YRDP’s project on promoting awareness-raising on Natural Resource Governance (NRG) and civic engagement then scaled up its interventions to youth engagement in policy influence for good governance and accountability. Over the last 6 years,YRDP has been an active member of the BWG, promoting awareness-raising among its target groups on national budget policy and publicfinancial management. YRDP engages youth across several platforms, where they can actively participate in advocacy actions by networks/like-minded partners, and working groups to improve and promote resource governance, transparency, and accountability. YRDP works in close collaboration with schools, teachers, universities, and local authorities through an action-oriented approach that strengthens youth leadership, civic engagement, and community participation. YRDP collaborate with various universities to refer and engage university students in joint YRDP activities, including volunteering, internships, youth leadership programs, and social action initiatives. Through these engagements, university students participate as active contributors and peer leaders, applying their academic knowledge to real community challenges while gaining practical experience in citizenship, advocacy, and social responsibility.
Intervention Design:The design of the CLIPS intervention complements the EU-funded SCOPE Public Financial Management (PFM) programme.While several interventions are similar in nature, CLIPSwill be implemented in different target locations to avoid duplication, maximise resource efficiency, and expand the overall reach and impact of public financial management reforms. Detailed activities are presented in the Annex (Logframe and Activity Matrix). CLIPS adopts a citizen-centred and systems-strengthening approach that promotes inclusive, transparent, and accountable public financial management at the sub-national level. Across all outcomes, the project integrates citizen-led accountability, participatory planning and budget monitoring, digital civic engagement, multi-stakeholder collaboration, and gender-responsive, inclusive, and environmentally sustainable governance. Civic engagement will be embedded within existing community and institutional structures to strengthen local ownership and ensure sustainability beyond the project period. The project will also strengthen linkages between local evidence and national policy dialogue, enabling lessons and citizen priorities from communes and districts to inform broader public financial management reforms. Outcome 1. Capacity and Participation: Strengthen the capacity of citizens and sub-national administrations to access, understand, and use budget information and digital participatory tools for effective engagement in local fiscal decision-making. Strategic Intervention: CLIPS will strengthen both the demand and supply sides of participatory public financial management by building citizens' knowledge and confidence while enhancing the capacity of sub-national administrations to facilitate inclusive and responsive engagement. The project combines institutional strengthening, capacity development, and digital civic engagement to improve access to information, foster constructive dialogue, and promote evidence-informed decision-making. Capacity development will be integrated into existing community organisations, youth networks, schools, and government systems to maximise sustainability and local ownership. The intervention will: • Establish adecentralised community of trainers by mobilising expertise from implementing partners and specialised organisations to deliver tailored training for youth, women, persons with disabilities (PwD), civil society organisations, journalists, and community representatives. • Strengthen citizens' knowledge and skills on public financial management, participatory planning, budgeting, budget monitoring, social accountability, and advocacy, enabling meaningful participation in Commune Investment Plans (CIP), Commune Development Plans (CDP), District Investment Plans (DIP), and District Development Plans (DDP). • Enhance the institutional capacity of sub-national administrations to facilitate inclusive and gender-responsive citizen engagement, integrate community priorities into planning and budgeting, and improve accountability and transparency. • Promote evidence-informed budget planning by strengthening the capacity of local authoritiesto use budget analysis and structured dialogue for more equitable and responsive resource allocation. • Expand digital civic engagement by promoting the use of existing public participation platforms, including the Citizens Budget, PIDOR, ISAF, and OWSO applications, to improve access to budget information, transparency, andcitizen feedback. Outcome 2. Accountability and Oversight: Strengthencitizen-led monitoring and accountability mechanisms to track public expenditure, promote transparency, and improve government responsiveness. Strategic Intervention: Building on strengthened capacities, CLIPS will support citizens to move beyond participation towards active leadership in accountability and oversight. The project will strengthen citizen-led monitoring, generate evidence for policy dialogue, and create institutionalopportunities for communities and government to jointly improve transparency, public expenditure management, and service delivery. Multi-stakeholder engagement will connect local accountability efforts with national policy advocacy and reform processes. Theintervention will: • Support community groups, youth networks, civil society organisations, and citizen monitors to design and implement citizen-led accountability initiatives on budgeting, procurement, public expenditure tracking,service delivery,andfiscal transparency. • Institutionalise participatory planning and budget monitoring by strengthening citizen engagement within formal local planning and decision-making processes, including Commune Investment Plans (CIP), Commune Development Plans (CDP),council meetings, and other accountability platforms. • Generate evidence for advocacy through community monitoring, budget analysis, action research, and citizen feedback mechanisms that inform dialogue with sub-national administrations and contributetonational policy advocacy and learning. • Foster a culture of civic engagement by integrating participatory governance and fiscal accountability into schools, youth networks, and community structures while supporting youth-led initiatives that promote transparency, inclusion, and accountable governance. Outcome 3. Institutionalisation and Sustainability: Institutionalise inclusive, transparent, and responsive mechanisms within sub-national administrations for sustained citizen participation. Strategic Intervention: CLIPSwill strengthen the enabling environment for participatory public financial management by supporting policy improvement, institutional adoption, and knowledge sharing. The project will embed participatory governance within governmentsystems and strengthen collaboration among communities, sub-national administrations, national institutions, and development partners to ensure that citizen participation becomes a routine feature of local governance beyond the project period. Theintervention will: • Review and strengthen policy frameworks, guidelines, and operational tools for civic engagement in public financial management, including the integration of digital participation approaches and inclusive governance principles withinlocalgovernment systems. • Support sub-national administrations to institutionalise participatory planning, budgeting, budget monitoring, and accountability mechanisms as part of routine governance processes. • Facilitate regular multi-stakeholder dialogueamong councils, citizens, civil society organisations, and national stakeholders to jointly analyse fiscal information, identify priorities, and strengthen evidence-based decision-making and policy advocacy. • Promote peer learning, documentation, and knowledgeexchange among communes, districts, national institutions, and development partners to facilitate replication, policy uptake, and long-term institutional sustainability. • Mainstream gender-responsive,disability-inclusive, youth-responsive, andenvironmentally sustainable governance approaches across policies, institutional practices, and participatory mechanisms to ensure equitable and resilient local development.

participating-org.narrative:
The YRDP was formally initiated in October 1992. In 1998 this program was legally registered with the Ministry of the Interior as alocal non-governmental youth organization. YRDP's mission is to strengthen Cambodian youth by developing their social conscience and enabling them to take responsibility for their own future and the future of their family, society and country.
Since 1992, about 40,000 students (42% are female) have participated in YRDP activities. Many are now working with different institutes, including private companies, civil society organizations, and government departments, as well as running their own businesses.
Currently, YRDP has four strategic programs: - Empowering Youth for an Equitable Society (Eyes) - Youth Engagement in Social Action (Yes Act) - YouthInvestment for Employment and Leadership Development (Yield) - Publication and Communication
